positions.title: NASA Space Academy Research Associate
positions.description: Conducted research related to heliophysics and solar weather prediction. Analyzed magnetogram data to determine measures to serve as the basis for new forecasting curves and determine their effectiveness at predicting solar weather events. Integrated these new measures into an existing tool: Magnetogram Forecast (MAG4). Used Iterative Data Language. Presented work to research supervisor on a weekly basis and gave a formal research talk. Co-authored paper to summarize our work.

positions.title: Information Technology Program Associate
positions.description: Information Technology Associates Program (ITAP) provides internship-quality opportunities for students to hone their technology and professional skills by working in selected on-campus jobs and projects involving technology. Through these experiences, ITAP interns gain valuable professional, communication, technology and leadership skills that will be essential to any career path, regardless of their major or area of study.

positions.title: Computer Science Research Assistant
positions.description: Conducted research related to embedded device security with funding from a National Science Foundation grant. Explored the hardware, software, and network security of commercial cable modems and routers. Used penetration testing to identify vulnerabilities and prepared reports detailing recommended mitigations for corporate distribution. Worked as a member of a three-person team on software design, implementation, and testing. Presented work to research supervisor on a weekly basis and also gave a formal research talk. Authored a paper to summarize our work.

positions.title: Mathematics Tutor
positions.description: Aid students in developing a strong mathematical foundation. Tutor in courses including Discrete Mathematics, Calculus, Analysis, and Operations Research.

positions.title: Computer Science Research Assistant
positions.description: Conducted research related to web browser security with funding from a National Science Foundation grant. Studied the security of several popular web browsers. Used JavaScript to enhance the security of Mozilla Firefox to combat common vulnerabilities and evaluated the functionality of the resulting system. Worked as a member of a three-person team on software design, implementation, and testing. Presented work to research supervisor on a weekly basis and also gave a formal research talk. Authored an abstract and a poster to summarize our work.

positions.title: Computer Science Instructor
positions.description: Taught classes of 8-16 students, ages 13-19. Taught topics including C++, Java, and Python. Mentored students as they designed, implemented, and debugged final projects.

volunteerExperiences.description: Volunteered to staff the museum on the weekends. Responsibilities included interacting with customers, working the register, answering phones, and organizing donations.

Volunteered with morning jazz band rehearsals, held once or twice every week. Led brass sectionals and assisted during full group rehearsals. Taught students the basic of jazz theory and improvisation.

projects.title: Data Visualization: Interacting with Financial Models
projects.description: Worked as part of a team to design and implement a visualization of a Financial Health Model. Consulted with the VP of Finance to identify the currently working models and to identify the desired functionality. Worked with Tableau Desktop and Tableau Reader to create an interactive visualization that is easily distributed to concerned parties. Presented work to the VP of Finance.

projects.title: SimpleIDE
projects.description: Worked independently to extend a Simple Integrated Developing Environment (IDE) for a simple functional language similar to SML. Created support for the interpretation of expressions, flow control statements, relational operators, function definitions, subroutine calls, and code module imports. Capstone project for Computer Science major. Worked with Scala and Eclipse. Presented work to computer science faculty and students.

organizations.name: Alpha Phi Omega, Alpha Upsilon Chapter
organizations.description: A nationally recognized co-ed service fraternity based on the values of leadership, friendship, and community service that seeks to provide students with an opportunity to engage in community service and learning essential leadership skills all within an atmosphere of friendship.

organizations.name: DePauw Computer Science Honorary Society
organizations.description: For junior and senior computer science majors, who are admitted on the basis of outstanding academic achievement in their computer science coursework.
